policy_text:
Conforming purchase loans, manual underwriting: eligibility rules (2026)
A loan application is approved only if it meets every rule below. Ratios are whole percentages rounded down. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when the file is silent on a point.

R1. After paying the cash needed to close, the borrower's assets including gifts must cover at least 6 months of the new housing payment.
R2. If the file does not mention a co-borrower living elsewhere, assume every borrower will live in the home.
R3. The debt-to-income ratio may not exceed 36%.
R4. The loan-to-value ratio (loan amount over property value) may not exceed 95%, unless the borrower is a first-time home buyer and the loan-to-value ratio is at most 97%.
R5. If a co-borrower will not live in the home, the loan-to-value ratio may not exceed 90%.
R6. Gift funds require a signed gift letter stating they do not have to be repaid.
R7. If first-time buyer status is not stated, treat the borrower as a repeat buyer.
R8. The representative credit score must be at least 640, unless the score is at least 620 and reserves after closing cover at least 6 months of the new payment.
R9. Monthly debts including the new housing payment may not exceed 43% of stable gross monthly income.

Remaining liquid funds are sufficient to cover 48 months of total monthly housing payments. Ownership records indicate that the applicant has held an interest in residential property within the past three years. The requested financing represents a loan-to-value ratio of 93%. The file contains no documentation of recent formal education or vocational training specific to the current profession. When factoring in the proposed housing obligation along with all liabilities, the total debt-to-income ratio is calculated at 40%. All individuals listed on the mortgage note will maintain primary occupancy of the subject property. Employment verification shows the applicant has accumulated 0 years of experience within this specific occupation. The settlement statement outlines a total cash requirement of $70,000 to finalize the purchase. Public records disclose a Chapter 7 bankruptcy that was legally discharged 1 year ago. The projected monthly housing expense, incorporating principal, interest, property taxes, hazard insurance, and applicable homeowner association dues, is $2,700. An analysis of W-2s, pay stubs, and federal tax returns verifies a stable gross monthly income of $7,000. An immediate family member is providing a financial contribution of $40,000 to assist with acquisition costs. The applicant is requesting a base mortgage amount of $300,000. The underwriting file provides no evidence of extenuating circumstances surrounding past credit difficulties. The subject property is situated in a county governed by standard conforming loan limits. Installment and revolving liabilities appearing on the credit bureau report require ongoing monthly payments of $150. A fully executed gift letter on file confirms that the transferred funds are provided as a non-repayable grant. The loan officer notes the borrower asked for a decision before school starts. The recognized collateral value is established at $320,000, representing the lesser of the agreed purchase price and the independent appraisal.

policy_text:
Conforming purchase loans, manual underwriting: eligibility rules (2026)
A loan application is approved only if it meets every rule below. Ratios are whole percentages rounded down. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when the file is silent on a point.

R1. After paying the cash needed to close, the borrower's assets including gifts must cover at least 1 months of the new housing payment.
R2. The loan-to-value ratio (loan amount over property value) may not exceed 90%.
R3. When the loan-to-value ratio is above 75%, the credit score must be at least 680.
R4. At least 7 years must have passed since a foreclosure was completed, unless extenuating circumstances are documented, at least 3 years have passed, and the loan-to-value ratio is at most 90%.
R5. A short sale must be at least 4 years old, or at least 2 years old with documented extenuating circumstances.
R6. The representative credit score must be at least 640, unless the score is at least 620 and reserves after closing cover at least 2 months of the new payment.
R7. The borrower must have at least 2 years of income history in the same line of work.
R8. The debt-to-income ratio may not exceed 36%. This rule does not apply if the credit score is at least 700, reserves cover at least 6 months, and the ratio is at most 45%.
R9. If the credit history section is silent, assume no bankruptcy, foreclosure or short sale.
R10. At least 4 years must have passed since a Chapter 7 bankruptcy was discharged.

Conforming purchase loans, manual underwriting: eligibility rules (2026)
A loan application is approved only if it meets every rule below. Ratios are whole percentages rounded down. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when the file is silent on a point.

R1. If the file does not mention a gift letter, treat it as having none.
R2. After paying the cash needed to close, the borrower's assets including gifts must cover at least 6 months of the new housing payment.
R3. If a co-borrower will not live in the home, the loan-to-value ratio may not exceed 90%.
R4. The loan-to-value ratio (loan amount over property value) may not exceed 95%.
R5. The debt-to-income ratio may not exceed 36%, unless the credit score is at least 720, reserves cover at least 6 months, and the ratio is at most 45%.
R6. The borrower must have at least 2 years of income history in the same line of work.
R7. The representative credit score must be at least 660. This rule does not apply if the score is at least 640 and reserves after closing cover at least 2 months of the new payment.
R8. If the file does not mention a co-borrower living elsewhere, assume every borrower will live in the home.
R9. The loan amount may not exceed the conforming limit of $806,500.
R10. Gift funds require a signed gift letter stating they do not have to be repaid.
R11. When the loan-to-value ratio is above 75%, the credit score must be at least 700.
case_text: File number 9164 contains the mortgage application submitted by applicant Elena Kowalczyk for a home purchase. The applicant is employed full-time as an intensive care unit nurse at a regional medical center. The applicant has never previously owned residential real estate. A fully executed donor document explicitly states that the provided funds carry no repayment obligation. Remaining liquid funds after closing are sufficient to cover 20 months of the upcoming mortgage obligation. She resides with and supports her two dependent children as a single parent. An attached personal statement mentions her routine attendance at a community mosque. On the derogatory credit section, the report lists a Chapter 7 bankruptcy discharged 3 years ago. The tri-merge credit report reflects a valid middle credit score of 660. Verification of employment confirms a duration of 3 years working within this specialized medical profession. The subject real estate is located within a recognized high-cost housing market county. The transaction does not involve any secondary applicant residing at another address. A total of $40,000 originating from family members is included in the available transaction funds. The applicant has not completed any recent educational programs or vocational training related to her current occupation. The established value for the real estate is $560,000, representing the lesser of the purchase price or the appraised value. The total funds required from the applicant at settlement equal $70,000. The resulting loan-to-value percentage for the mortgage financing is 53%. Supplied paperwork demonstrates that the prior credit blemish was caused by an unexpected termination of employment beyond the applicant's influence. The requested mortgage financing principal is $300,000. Combined balances across checking, savings, and eligible retirement portfolios equal $80,000. Processing notes indicate the applicant requested status updates prior to the start of the academic term. The projected monthly housing expense, incorporating principal, interest, property taxes, hazard insurance, and homeowners association fees, is $2,400. Creditor liabilities appearing on the report require ongoing monthly payments of $1,200.
